reasons: F01, F02, F03: a material weakness is disclosed and there is no auditor attestation on internal control, so the control environment looks weak and has not been tested by the auditor; this profile is typical of a small company.

F04, F19, F21, R16: going-concern doubt, a covenant breach, waiver or amendment, and a capital raise in the year or planned (securities were issued) mean heavy financing pressure and a reason to make results look better.
F12, F13, F11: one customer makes up 100% of revenue and receivables, and related-party transactions are material, which raises the risk that some sales are not arm's-length or not real.

F05, F25, F28: a change of auditor within two years, a voluntary accounting change and a segment or reporting change all increase the risk of accounting judgement and of results being hard to compare across years.

R04, R14, R01, R02: sales fell about 98% (SGI 0.02, cash sales -0.83), and both DSRI (2.62) and GMI (1.87) rose sharply; this looks like a business in collapse, although the indices are skewed by the tiny revenue base.
R08, R10, R09: accruals are high (TATA 0.22, RSST 0.20) and the Beneish M-score of -0.25 is well above the -1.78 threshold, though the M-score is inflated by the revenue collapse.

R17, R19, R07, F16, F17, F18, F07: offsetting this, the F-score of 0.16 is below 1.0, operating cash flow is 1.68 times net income, leverage fell, there are no SEC or other investigations or class actions, and no prior-period correction, so the main risk looks like distress and going concern rather than a confirmed misstatement.
